newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end lower on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end lower on profit taking.

text.p: The Jakarta stock index fell on broad profit-taking on Monday, but brokers said interest in car maker Astra kept it from a steep decline.
The composite index fell 5.09 points, or 0.89 percent, to close at 566.25 after touching a low for the day of 565.40 points in late trade. Losers led gainers by 71 to 26, with 53 counters unchanged.
"Selling pressure is likely to continue on Tuesday as most investors are awaiting the initial public offering of BNI (state Bank Negara Indonesia) next week," one broker said.
BNI will offer 1.1 billion shares at 850 rupiah each for four days from November 4 ahead of their November 25 listing on the Jakarta and Surabaya exchanges.
"We are even receiving orders from Singapore to buy BNI shares at 10 percent above the offer price. It is seen to be oversubscribed," a foreign analyst said.

"The sluggish trade on Monday was also due to the absence of foreign participation. With the approach of the year-end, many foreign fund managers are evaluating their portfolios in Indonesia for the coming year," another foreign analyst said.
Vehicle manufacturer Astra International made significant gains despite weak market sentiment due to active buying on its fundamentals coupled with speculative interest, brokers said.

They said there was speculation that some existing Astra shareholders intended to increase their stakes on the market. It rose 125 rupiah to 4,075 rupiah, with about 2.3 million shares changing hands after it rose to 4,175 rupiah in early trade.
Fisheries firm Daya Guna Samudra topped the active list with 6.4 million shares traded, falling 100 rupiah to 2,125 rupiah.
Brokers said it was due to locally-led profit-taking after its encouraging debut last week.
Toll road operator Citra Marga fell 100 rupiah to 1,700 on a turnover of 3.3 million shares, also due to profit-taking.
Brokers said the market had anticipated the profit-taking as investors were mostly trading on a short-term basis.
"They want to use the money for the BNI IPO because the offer price is relatively cheap compared to other banks," said one local broker.
